title: Enterprise SDK intake: prioritization rubric for resumable streaming, token rotation, and multi-lang support
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: We need a repeatable, lightweight triage rubric and intake workflow for enterprise customer requests around client SDKs and client libraries. Focus areas for this ticket: (1) resumable/robust streaming ergonomics (reconnect/backpressure/resume), (2) enterprise auth patterns (rotating tokens, SSO/OIDC, cert-based/mTLS), and (3) additional language support priorities (Rust/Go/Swift). The outcome should be a prioritized backlog with scoring, an intake form template for Solutions/CS, and clear acceptance criteria for engineering handoff. Rationale: Over the last two quarters we received ~24 enterprise tickets that fall into this surface; ad hoc handling has led to inconsistent solutions, rework, and missed SLAs. This rubric will reduce triage time and give stakeholders predictable expectations.
proposed_work: Draft scoring rubric (cost to implement, estimated developer effort, security exposure, customer revenue impact, number of customers requesting, compatibility with hosted/dedicated/private),

Prototype a one-page intake form for Solutions/CS that enforces required fields (customer context, security posture, required languages/platforms, desired streaming semantics, SLA/throughput expectations),
Run a 2-week intake pilot with 5 queued customer requests and apply rubric to produce prioritized backlog,
Convene a 60-minute cross-functional review (SDK eng, Platform, Security, Solutions) to review pilot results and finalize rubric,
Produce a PRD and a GitHub epic with sub-issues for the top 3 prioritized items (e.g., resumable streaming API, token rotation helper lib, Rust SDK bootstrap).
acceptance_criteria: A documented rubric exists in Confluence with scoring examples applied to 5 real customer requests,
A templated intake form in Drive that includes security/sign-off fields and mandatory fields for streaming semantics,
At least one prioritized GitHub epic created with clear engineering acceptance criteria and estimates,
Pilot review notes with recorded decisions and next steps, and Security has indicated whether a formal review is required for each item.
Ship-plan for top-priority item (owner, estimate, target release) agreed in review meeting.

notes: Trade-offs: Doing language bindings increases maintenance surface; consider a generic gRPC/HTTP reference with generated bindings vs. handwritten idiomatic libraries.

We should avoid changing serving runtime wire semantics where possible to reduce rollout friction for Dedicated/Private deployments; prefer client-side helpers and small opt-in server-side resume token support.
Measure success: reduce average triage time from ~3 days to <24 hours for SDK requests, reduce rework cycles by 50% in next quarter.
